transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-21
Time: 08:47 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Samir Khan (Redwood CSM), Maria Gonzales (Finovo Head of AI), Ethan Park (Finovo Platform), Siva Raman (Finovo Security), Leah Cole (Finovo Product)

Summary:
- Main goal: plan canary + rollout for the POC -> go-live cutover. Confirm monitoring, runbooks, rollback triggers, and timing.
- Agreed to run a dry-run cutover on 2025-10-28, finalize canary traffic split and runbook this week.

Topics:
- Canary strategy and traffic split (5-10% initial)
- A/B vs canary for feature gating
- Monitoring dashboards and SLOs (p99 latency, error rate)
- Rollback triggers and automated fallback to hosted model
- Compliance/runbook sign-off and change window

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan Lee: Okay folks, thanks for joining. we have 45 minutes, main agenda is canary + cutover planning. Priya, can you kickoff with the canary proposal?
00:12 Priya Raman: Sure, yeah. so the recommended approach from Redwood is a two-phase canary. start with 5% of traffic for 24 hours, evaluate latency and error rate, then bump to 20% for 6 hours, then full switch if everything is green. the canary will run on dedicated pool nodes we provisioned for the POC \u001A that gives predictable latency.
00:40 Maria Gonzales: Quick question, why dedicated rather than hosted? we thought hosted would be simpler.
00:46 Priya Raman: Good question. for the go-live profile you gave us (high concurrencies, 500qps burst), dedicated gives better p99 guarantees and you get isolation for PCI-sensitive payloads. hosted could work but latency may vary and there are tenancy limits; we recommended dedicated for the initial cutoff and then assess cost tradeoffs post-cutover.
01:05 Ethan Park: That makes sense; cost is a concern though, do you have a cost delta for the dedicated canary period?
01:12 Jordan Lee: I'll share the pricing delta after this call; roughly for the dedicated pool during the 48-hour canary window you're looking at an uplift of ~X%. exact numbers in the email. 
01:24 Priya Raman: Also we can reduce cost by enabling quantization profile Q2 for inference which keeps quality within your eval thresholds \u001A that reduces GPU utilization. we'll include that in the runbook.
01:40 Leah Cole: On the A/B vs canary note, our PM recommends A/B to compare quality between current model and new model. is that doable?
01:48 Priya Raman: Yes, you can do an A/B within the canary. run a weighted A/B where 5% of overall traffic splits into 50/50 between old and new model variants; that gives you quality comparison while limiting exposure. some telemetry needs be instrumented to flag regressions on prompts in your eval set.
02:12 Maria Gonzales: Ok great. what monitoring are we expected to have? we want clear smoke signals.
02:18 Priya Raman: We'll provide Redwood Console dash with per-route p50/p95/p99, token cost, error rate, latency histograms, and a quality regression dashboard tied to your prompt set. Alerts: p99 > 600ms for more than 5 minutes, or error rate > 1% for 2 minutes, or quality regression on golden prompts > threshold.
02:42 Siva Raman: For security and compliance, we need audit logs, KMS key usage, and proof that model inputs aren't retained beyond retention window. can you confirm encryption in flight and at rest?
02:55 Jordan Lee: Yes, TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest, KMS integration for keys \u001A we'll share SOC2 docs and the KMS diagram. retention policy set to 30 days for POC logs unless you request shorter.
03:12 Siva Raman: We need runbook steps enumerated with owners. also need a fail-closed path if rollback is required to guarantee no partial state.
03:20 Priya Raman: Runbook will include step-by-step: pre-cutover checklist, smoke tests, traffic steering commands, rollback commands (automated fallback to hosted model or previous variant), and contact matrix. we'll mark the trigger thresholds and automation we can run for rollback.
03:38 Ethan Park: about rollback automation, does the runtime have automatic fallback if latency spikes?
03:44 Priya Raman: Yes, we have an automated fallback policy option \u001A if p99 exceeds threshold or error rates spike, traffic is automatically redirected to the previous stable variant or to a lower-cost hosted fallback. we need to agree on thresholds and which fallback to use.
04:00 Maria Gonzales: For the dry-run on 10/28, what exactly are we testing?
04:04 Jordan Lee: Dry-run will simulate the traffic shift in staging using a replay of last week's production requests and run the smoke checks. we won't change production DNS or traffic, it's a rehearsal. the actual cutover window is target 11/03 weekend (tentative) pending sign-offs.
04:20 Leah Cole: Who owns the sign-off? our security team plus Finovo product and Redwood AE?
04:25 Samir Khan: Typically sign-off = Finovo security (Siva), Finovo product (Leah), and Redwood CSM (Samir) for operational readiness. We'll note that in the runbook.
04:40 Siva Raman: On compliance, we also need the ability to run an audit log export and a pre-signed snapshot of the runbook for our records.
04:48 Jordan Lee: We'll provide an exportable audit bundle and a timestamped runbook PDF.
04:53 Maria Gonzales: A couple nitty-gritty items \u001A KV cache cold start behavior when we flip models, any advice?
04:58 Priya Raman: Good catch. switching model weights will invalidate KV caches for the older model; we recommend warming the cache in canary by sending synthetic warmup traffic reflective of prefix distribution. add warmup steps to the pre-cutover checklist; that reduces initial latency spikes.
05:20 Ethan Park: Instrumentation: can you expose per-token cost and attribution per route so we can track cost during canary?
05:26 Priya Raman: Yes. Redwood Console exposes token-level cost breakdown per route and model. we'll share a dashboard link and set a watch.
05:34 Maria Gonzales: Any gotchas around SSO / SAML during the cutover? we use Okta.
05:40 Jordan Lee: Okta SSO is already integrated in your tenant; for the canary nothing changes there. if we need to spin up separate service accounts for the dedicated pool we will create them and add them to your Okta group \u001A we'll document steps.
05:56 Leah Cole: How about canary window length again? you said 24h then 6h?
06:00 Priya Raman: Correct: 5% for 24 hours, evaluate signals; then 20% for 6 hours. if no blockers, proceed to ramp to 100% with a controlled ramp (50% -> 100% over 1 hour). all subject to signoffs.
06:18 Maria Gonzales: I want a hard rollback if quality regresses on our golden prompts \u001A immediate rollback, manual sign-off for reattempt.
06:24 Priya Raman: We'll set that as a hard trigger: if quality delta exceeds X on golden set, we immediately cut traffic back to previous variant and alert the team.
06:33 Ethan Park: Are there any infra changes we need in our VPC for the dedicated pool?
06:38 Priya Raman: Minimal. we need a eks nodegroup security group rule to allow the pool to reach your data endpoints if you keep private callbacks; otherwise calls are outbound to Redwood. we'll share exact firewall rules.
06:50 Samir Khan: Action item summary: Priya will draft runbook; Jordan will send pricing and SOC2 docs; Ethan to confirm change window; Siva to review runbook; everyone to join dry-run on 10/28.
07:05 Maria Gonzales: Sounds good. a little worried about cost but acceptable for initial launch.
07:10 Jordan Lee: Understood \u001A we'll include cost optimization suggestions post-go-live (batching, caching policies).
07:18 Leah Cole: One last question, how do we handle user-visible errors during canary? do we surface a fallback message?
07:24 Priya Raman: We recommend graceful degradation: on gateway error return a cached response or a soft failure message. that's in the runbook plus in-app UX guidance.
07:33 Maria Gonzales: Okay thanks. let's recap next steps and owners.
07:38 Jordan Lee: Recap: finalize runbook (Priya), pricing & compliance docs (Jordan), confirm change window (Ethan), security signoff (Siva), dry-run 10/28. We'll circulate minutes and attach the runbook draft.
07:55 Maria Gonzales: Thanks everyone.
07:57 Jordan Lee: Thanks folks. meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription quality: Some speaker overlaps and a couple of product names were mis-transcribed (e.g., "Red wood" heard once). There are a few filler words and short crosstalks.
